title: Support for Incarcerated Singaporeans to Help Dependants Seek Assistance
what_it_is: Support for Incarcerated Singaporeans to Help Dependants Seek Assistance

sections.label: Family support for inmates
sections.summary: FRCs at Prison Link Centre work with MSF and partners to assess inmates' families' needs and refer them to community resources.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Family members may also approach the FRCs directly, which are located at the Prison Link Centre where family members go to visit the inmates.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: FRCs will work with the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) and community partners to look into the inmates' requests.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: In addition, inmates with children below 21 years old and elderly dependants above 60 years old are proactively identified by SPS under the Early Triaging Process upon their admission into prison.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: With the inmate's consent, trained social workers from SPS' FRCs will assess the family's needs and refer them to appropriate community resources.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: As for inmates who join the Yellow Ribbon Community Project, grassroots volunteers will engage their family members to offer befriending support and link them to community resources.

sections.label: Engaging families and community partners
sections.summary: Stakeholders continue engaging families, and those suspecting loved ones are crime victims can approach community partners or Police.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: In order to reach to the families, it may not be easy, but the stakeholders continue to engage day by day, sometimes, we make many calls – all with the purpose of caring for fellow Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: So, I want to assure the Member that we will continue to strengthen this ecosystem and at the same time, whenever there is any one suspecting that their loved ones outside, who may be affected, like being a victim to a crime, they can approach any of the community partners, they can also go to the local Police set-up and we will work together whenever we get any information, so that we protect each of us here in Singapore.
